newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ dlr closes weaker after CPI comes in on f'cast.
newsitem.headline: NZ dlr closes weaker after CPI comes in on f'cast.

text.p: The New Zealand dollar closed weaker on Tuesday, even though key inflation data failed to provide the market with the excuse it was looking for to sell the currency agressively, dealers said.
The Kiwi closed at US$0.6648/58, down from 0.6660/65 at the open.

After the release of CPI data this morning, the Reserve bank calculated that underlying inflation was at 0.3 percent in the June quarter and 1.49 percent in the June year, exactly in line with the bank's and economists' forecasts.
"The market had been pre-empting probably an easier number. Even though the economists were forecasting 0.3 percent, I think the market wanted to see a lower number," said a senior Wellington dealer.
"It wasn't to be, it came out on expectations. We had a moderate short squeeze, but I think it's just a reflection of the overwhelming bearish sentiment that it failed to sustain that squeeze."
He said the firmer greenback was helping to buoy the Trade-Weighted Index and keep monetary conditions relatively stable in the face of the weaknening Kiwi.
The TWI closed at 65.82 from 65.81 at the open.
"And as long as that continues, there's no problem in terms of the level of monetary conditions," the dealer said.
"I think we'll see an orderly depreciation continue, and certinaly the market will keep a wary eye on the level of the MCI."
The Monetary Conditions Index (MCI) closed at 762 -- 63 points below the Reserve Bank's desired level and 13 points outside its 50-point comfort zone.
Dealers said the bank was probably happy with conditions at the current level and was unlikely to take any action unless the MCI fell to 70 points below its desired level.
The Kiwi was seen trading in a 0.6640-70 range overnight.
